verdict.rationale: Hyperbrowser is built to be driven headlessly and programmatically: cloud browser sessions are controlled through Playwright/Puppeteer/CDP or official SDKs, agent tasks start with a single API call, and an `hx` CLI exists. However, nothing documents CI pipelines specifically, and the CLI is only shown for sandboxes, so the CI half of the story is implied rather than demonstrated. missing for 10: documented CI pipeline integration (e.g., GitHub Actions examples or CI auth/secrets guidance), CLI coverage beyond sandboxes, independent hands-on corroboration of CI usage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Sessions are isolated browser instances running in the cloud that you can control programmatically. Each session gives you a WebSocket endpoint to connect with Playwright, Puppeteer, or any CDP-compatible tool.
you can start tasks with a single API call and watch them execute live.
Control Chrome browsers in the cloud using Puppeteer, Playwright, or our SDKs—no infrastructure management required.
Set up the Hyperbrowser CLI (`hx`) and/or the SDKs to start working with sandboxes.
Connect your existing automation scripts to cloud browsers
